FEES & BEST PRACTICES GUIDELINES

5.1 PREPARATION FEES
If a private medical practitioner * supplies a witness, the guidelines to the fees claimable are:

a. Trial preparation (review of medical notes)                  $100 to $200
b. Trial preparation (review of medical notes, including research, $200 to $400 per hour
   discussion with instructing lawyer, preparation of affidavit etc)

GUIDELINES FOR PHYSICIANS AND INSURANCE COMPANIES
This Committee would like to remind physicians and insurance companies to observe the following procedure in order to ensure the smooth processing of medical reports.

a. A written request for the medical report should be submitted to the doctor by the company indicating the purpose and the provision of the report.
b. The company must request the physician to provide a copy of the original medical report and any additional laboratory reports to be forwarded.
c. The physician must first obtain the patient's consent, but upon receipt of payment, the report should be provided within 2 weeks.
d. Insurance companies should not withdraw a request for a report after a physician has agreed to provide the report.

GUIDELINES ON MEDICAL REPORTS REQUESTED BY LAWYERS
a. A written request for medical report must be obtained.
b. The purpose of the medical report must be stated.
c. The request should specify the length of the report.
d. If the medical request is for medico-legal purpose, the patient should be referred to the clinic or hospital for a medico-legal examination.
e. There must be a written consent from the patient to waive confidentiality.
